n: Gashapon Department Store Ikebukuro Main Store (ガシャポンのデパート 池袋総本店)
w: Bandai Namco's capsule-toy flagship — about 3,000 gashapon machines across 1,256 m², the most at any single location — dispensing Pokémon, Gundam, Ultraman and Doraemon figures, mostly ¥200–¥300.
anime: Gashapon culture — Bandai's world-record capsule-toy store, stocked with anime and game character figures
gs: Wikipedia published coordinates — Sunshine City, Tokyo (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunshine_City,_Tokyo); the store is inside the complex
sts: Bandai Namco official store page + Time Out, seen 2026-10-02

n: Tokyo Character Street, Tokyo Station (東京キャラクターストリート)
address: First Avenue Tokyo Station B1 (Yaesu side), 1-9-1 Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
w: An underground row of 30-plus official character shops opened in 2008 on the Yaesu side of Tokyo Station — Pokémon, Studio Ghibli, Kirby, Chiikawa, Crayon Shin-chan, Rilakkuma and Hello Kitty, some with station-exclusive goods.
anime: Character merchandise — one corridor of official stores for Pokémon, Ghibli, Kirby, Shin-chan, Chiikawa and more
gs: Wikipedia published coordinates — Tokyo Station (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Station); the street is in the station's Yaesu-side basement mall

n: Oizumi Anime Gate, Ōizumi-gakuen (大泉アニメゲート)
address: North-exit pedestrian deck, Ōizumi-gakuen Station (Seibu Ikebukuro Line), Nerima-ku, Tokyo
w: Opened in 2015 outside Ōizumi-gakuen Station: life-size bronze statues of Astro Boy, Joe Yabuki (Ashita no Joe), Tetsurō and Maetel (Galaxy Express 999) and Lum (Urusei Yatsura) — Nerima's tribute to itself as the birthplace of Japanese TV animation.
anime: Nerima 'Anime City' — home of Toei Animation and Mushi Production (Astro Boy, Japan's first TV anime series); statues of Astro Boy, Joe, Maetel and Lum
gs: Wikipedia published coordinates — Ōizumi-gakuen Station (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Cizumi-gakuen_Station); the gate is on the station's north-exit deck
sts: GO TOKYO spot page (permanent public installation), seen 2026-10-02
